name: Adani Power Ltd.
business_summary: India's largest private thermal generator: ~18 GW operating (plant list per model knowledge: Mundra, Mahan, Tiroda, Kawai, Raipur, Raigarh, Udupi, Godda for Bangladesh), 24 GW pipeline under construction/awarded (62% tied under long-term PPAs; target ~45 GW by 2032), plus Bhutan hydro JVs and the 330 MW Alaknanda hydro (via GVK Energy CIRP). Q2 FY27: sales volume 26.4 bn units (+11.5%), PLF 70.1%, continuing revenue Rs 17,014 cr (+29.8%), continuing EBITDA Rs 6,321 cr (+18.5%), reported PAT Rs 7,019 cr (+142%, includes Rs 2,422 cr one-time prior-period revenue from Gujarat PPA energy-charge revisions). Debt Rs 61,860 cr, net Rs 45,846 cr; rated AA+. Promoters 74.96%; mcap Rs 3.94 lakh cr, P/E 21.7.

revenue_mix.segment: Long/medium-term PPAs (23.4 bn of 26.4 bn units)
revenue_mix.geography: India (Gujarat, Maharashtra, Haryana, Rajasthan, UP, Bihar) + Bangladesh (Godda)

exposures.mechanism: Merchant/short-term volumes were 11% of Q2 sales (26.4 bn units total; 23.4 bn under PPAs) and short-term tariffs rose 33% YoY. Merchant revenue ~Rs 2,200 cr/qtr (est. ~3.0 bn units x ~Rs 7.3) = ~13% of continuing revenue; +15% spot => +Rs 330 cr/qtr = Rs 1,320 cr/yr = +5.2% on continuing EBITDA ~Rs 25k cr (H1 13.3k x2); merchant share is falling as capacity is tied under medium-term PPAs, so x persistence 0.4 and EV/MCap 1.12 => +2.3.

evidence.note: Merchant and short-term volume 43% lower YoY as capacity tied up; short-term merchant tariffs +33% per unit
Mcap Rs 3.94 lakh cr; net debt Rs 45,846 cr (call)

exposures.mechanism: Q2 demand +11.5% YoY to 502 bn units drove Adani's PLF to 70.1% (62.8% LY) and volumes +11.5%; EBITDA continuing +18.5%. PPAs pay fixed capacity charges regardless, but incremental dispatch earns energy-charge margin and incentives, and frees merchant sales. +3pp demand => ~+4% volume (PLF +2.5pp) = 4.2 bn units/yr x ~Rs 1.8/unit margin = Rs 760 cr = +2.9% EBITDA x 1.12 x persistence 0.5 => +1.6.

evidence.note: Power demand +11.5% to 502 BU in Q2; thermal PLF 68% vs 62%; Adani PLF 70.1% vs 62.8%
Coal stocks at power plants critically low as demand surges

exposures.mechanism: Q2 power demand rose with a 13% monsoon deficit (cooling load) and hydro generation fell ~15%, so coal/lignite supplied 73% of incremental generation (call). A +10% monsoon swing reverses part of this: demand growth -2pp and hydro +10% displaces ~3 bn units/qtr of thermal; at Adani's ~7% share of thermal generation, volume -1.5% => EBITDA ~-1.8% (variable margin) x 1.12 x 0.8 persistence (seasonal, 2 quarters) => -2.0.

evidence.note: Lower hydropower output because of weak monsoons; coal and lignite supplied 73% of incremental generation
JSW call: monsoon ~13% below normal in Q2 FY27, hydro generation -15% (cross-check)

exposures.mechanism: Landed cost of imported coal rose ~50% YoY (call); fuel cost Q2 Rs 10,229 cr (+41.8%) = 60% of continuing revenue. Imported-coal plants (Mundra ~4.6 GW, Udupi etc. - model knowledge) are ~25-30% of fuel spend (est. Rs 2.8k cr/qtr). +15% coal => +Rs 430 cr/qtr cost. Pass-through: Bangladesh (Godda) tariff reflects international prices immediately; Gujarat PPAs index with a lag of >6 months (hit in Q3, mgmt); merchant prices rise with coal. Net 55% recovered over a year => unrecovered 45% = Rs 780 cr/yr = -3.0% EBITDA, x1.12 x persistence 0.3 => -1.0, offset +0.5 for merchant uplift on domestic-coal plants => -0.5. Pack empirical is +3.60 (t +1.6): opposite sign and likely driven by shared tight-power cycle; central value kept near zero with a wide range.

evidence.note: Landed imported coal cost +~50%; Gujarat indexation lag >6 months; Bangladesh PPA gets immediate pass-through
Pack empirical F_COAL_INTL +3.60 per SSU, t +1.6

exposures.mechanism: Domestic coal (linkage + e-auction) fuels ~70% of capacity. Coal India has not raised notified prices, but effective cost rose in Q2 on poorer quality (monsoon), not recovered in tariffs in the quarter. +10% domestic coal cost on ~Rs 6k cr/qtr domestic fuel = Rs 600 cr/qtr; ~85% passes through under Section 62 / escalable-energy-charge PPAs after a lag => unrecovered 15% = Rs 360 cr/yr = -1.4% EBITDA x 1.12 x 0.6 => -1.0.

evidence.note: Coal India has not increased notified prices; effective cost slightly higher due to lower quality in Q2
Domestic coal stocks at multi-year lows

exposures.mechanism: P/E 21.7, EV/MCap 1.12, net debt only ~Rs 46k cr (net debt/EBITDA ~1.8x) so lower duration than renewables peers; growth capex of 24 GW pipeline (~Rs 1.5 lakh cr) funded mostly by internal accruals. +25bp on a ~10% WACC with equity duration ~10 => -2.5; PPAs partly index to cost of debt => -1.8.

evidence.note: CFO: capex funded primarily through internal accruals; net debt Rs 45,846 cr; AA+ rating upgrade
RBI hiked repo 25 bp to 5.50% on 7 Oct 2026, first hike in ~4 years; stance calibrated tightening; cuts 'off the table' (Reuters, The Hindu, Business Standard headlines)

exposures.mechanism: Total debt Rs 61,860 cr (net Rs 45,846 cr) of which ~50% floating (estimate); +25bp = Rs 77 cr/yr vs H1 finance costs Rs 1,662 cr and TTM PBT Rs 20.5k cr = -0.4% PAT; flows through to equity value only via cost of new project debt on the Rs 1.5 lakh cr programme: 40% debt-funded x 25bp x capitalised = ~-1.2% of mcap at EV/MCap 1.12.

evidence.note: Total debt Rs 61,860 cr (Sep-26) vs Rs 53,556 cr (Mar-26); finance cost H1 Rs 1,662 cr
RBI hiked repo 25 bp to 5.50% on 7 Oct 2026, first hike in ~4 years; stance calibrated tightening; cuts 'off the table' (Reuters, The Hindu, Business Standard headlines)

exposures.mechanism: Upgraded to AA+ by CARE and India Ratings in Q2 FY27, so spread beta is lower than other Adani names; +50bp on Rs 20k cr refinancing over 2 yrs = Rs 100 cr/yr = -0.5% PAT; plus access risk => -1.2.

evidence.note: Credit rating upgraded from AA to AA+ (CARE, India Ratings)

exposures.mechanism: Imported coal costs in USD (rupee +3% => +Rs 85 cr/qtr cost, partially passed through) vs Bangladesh Godda 1,600 MW PPA billed in USD (~7% of revenue => +Rs 40 cr/qtr) and merchant uplift. Net unrecovered ~ -0.5% EBITDA x 1.12 x 0.4 persistence... => -0.6 incl. capex import content (BHEL local; boilers local). Pack empirical -2.17 (t -1.0) is consistent in sign and larger.

evidence.note: Bangladesh PPA tariff determined on international prices; imported-coal cost increase
Pack empirical F_USDINR -2.17 per SSU, t -1.0

exposures.mechanism: Counterparties are state discoms (Maharashtra, Haryana, Rajasthan, UP, Bihar, Uttarakhand) and Bangladesh; faster discom reform and tighter late-payment rules lift realisation and allow 62%-tied long-term PPAs for the 24 GW pipeline. +1 SSU => PPA win rate and collection improve; assumed +2% of mcap.

evidence.note: Long-term PPAs secured for 62% of 24 GW pipeline; 1,320 MW 25-yr PPA from Uttarakhand (Korba-2); 1,600 MW Raipur-III for Maharashtra discom

exposures.mechanism: Stronger RE/storage support erodes midday thermal PLF and shifts bids to FDRE; but India now plans >100 GW new thermal by 2032 (CEA Chair cited; mgmt) and energy-security policy favours coal baseload, so substitution risk is mostly in long-dated PPAs. -0.8 per +1 SSU.

evidence.note: Mgmt: India needs >100 GW new thermal by 2032; CEA chairman statement on capacity beyond 97 GW target

exposures.mechanism: Round-the-clock load from data centres is thermal-friendly (RTC PPAs); 1,600 MW Raipur-III is for a second Maharashtra RTC PPA. +1 SSU => +1 GW thermal PPA demand over 2 yrs ~ +Rs 3k cr NPV (0.8% mcap) x 1.12 x ... => +1.5 incl. sentiment.

evidence.note: Raipur expansion Phase III 1,600 MW to supply second long-term PPA to Maharashtra discom

exposures.mechanism: Hormuz disruption pushes Asia to coal, lifts imported coal and merchant power prices, and raises energy-security priority of domestic coal baseload (positive for dispatch and PPA awards) but raises imported-fuel cost on Mundra-type plants (negative until pass-through). Net slightly positive.

evidence.note: Middle East conflict disrupting LNG/crude via Hormuz; Asia pivoting to coal (Wood Mackenzie 12 Oct, EnergyNow 3 Nov 2026 headlines)
Over half of coal plants at critically low stocks; captive plants ordered to maximise output from 1 Oct (Times of India 21 Oct, Reuters 28 Sep 2026 headlines)

exposures.mechanism: Beta ~1.0 (pack); FII 11.0%, DII 4.5%, retail holders 2.18 mn; +US$5bn quarterly inflow ~ +2% Nifty x beta 1.0 x 0.9 => +1.8.

evidence.note: Shareholding Sep-26: promoters 74.96%, FIIs 11.03%, DIIs 4.47%

company_links.mechanism: Adani family holds 74.96%. Group sell-offs (Jan 2023, Nov 2024) and relief rallies (US case dismissed 10 Aug 2026) moved Adani Power along with the group, although its larger operating cash flow (P/E 22) makes it the least group-sensitive of the Adani utilities. Judgement estimate.

evidence.note: US criminal case against Gautam Adani dismissed 10-11 Aug 2026
